Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: C
Q2: REFRAME
Q3: B

RATIONALE:
Q1: Option A needs the shard 1 `FAIL` line, and I can't supply it. I can't reach the run, and the triage issue says the full job log was not available to it either. Picking A without the data would loop clarification again, so the data-provision guard rules it out. Option B claims an infrastructure flake, and nothing in the evidence supports that. C, which goes ahead without the log, is the honest choice.
Q2: Option A only works if the fix run can check out PR #6910's head (`74c000f4`). It can't. Fixes from triage issues are built from the default branch: the triage body strips the routing lines, and `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:84-85,687-688` shows which lines it strips. The fix sandbox only has the files of the checked-out commit and no network. A's goal still holds: reproduce first, and fix only what reproduces. So I reframe A to run against the checked-out tree. The only change PR #6910 makes is missing-`jq` skips in two tests, and `main` doesn't have them yet (the only `jq` lookup in `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` is at line 2849). Option C is held back as the end state if nothing reproduces.
Q3: This issue carries no routing line (`Integration branch:` / `Target branch:`), so the pipeline will branch `ai/issue-<this issue>` from `main` and open the PR against `main`. Option A can't be reached from this issue without inventing routing data. A defect fixed on `main` reaches PR #6910 the next time `main` is merged into it, and the review workflow already does that merge for conflicts and for the merge train.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q2:
  strategy: reframe
  inputs:
    - `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1304-1334`: how the test list is built (top-level `test_*` functions, sorted, minus the `test_implementation_failed_*` fast-fail set).
    - `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1371-1408`: the two-level `NR % total == n` split, with 4 groups and `CI_POLL_TEST_SHARDS` defaulting to 4. Group index 3 and shard 1 are what failed.
    - `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`, which runs the selected tests when given their names as arguments.
    - `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`. Edit it only if a reproduced failure shows a defect in the poller.
  steps:
    - Build the list with the exact Python snippet from `ci.yml:1307-1334`, then the group 3 subset (`awk -v n=3 -v total=4 'NR % total == n'`), then the shard 1 subset (`awk -v n=1 -v total=4 'NR % total == n'`). Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py <shard tests>`.
    - Run the other three group 3 shards as well. Test names on `main` may sort differently from the PR head, so this covers the test that failed in CI even if it moved to another shard.
    - Check whether `jq` is on PATH and record the result. PR #6910 only adds missing-`jq` skips, so a missing `jq` would point to that cause.
    - If a test fails consistently: fix the assertion or the poller defect at its root cause, then re-run the same slice until it passes.
    - If nothing fails, or the sandbox can't run it (no `jq`, can't start bash): make no code change and report, as the outcome, that the failure did not reproduce, listing the test names and the sandbox limits. Under the auto-fix cap, generation 3 of 3 is the last one, so the next CI failure on PR #6910 goes to a human rather than another triage issue.
    - Never weaken the CI gate (`ci.yml` shard or aggregate failure handling, the `lint` aggregate). Never add a skip, `continue-on-error`, or retry without evidence from a reproduced run.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "Inspect the complete shard 1 log for its FAIL line" and "rebuild the shard list from PR #6910's head".
  equivalence_argument: CI ran the same test module with the same partitioning. Running the whole of group 3 on the checked-out tree covers every test that could have been in the failing shard 1, and only reproduced failures lead to code changes. That matches the issue's rule: fix only if it reproduces, otherwise re-run CI.
  reversibility: If a human later finds the real shard 1 log, they can file a targeted fix. When nothing reproduces, no code has changed, so there is nothing to undo.

SETUP REQUIRED (only when a decision relies on a placeholder):
- None.

Assumptions: fixes from triage issues are built from the default branch because the triage body strips routing lines; I inferred this from `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:13,84-85,687-688`. The fix sandbox has only the files of the checked-out commit and no network, as described in agents.md under "Isolated Codex agents".
